title: Hybrid swarm kernel selector with length & attention-phase probing
creator: Nina Patel
description: Problem: Our current kernel pickers use static heuristics and lightweight bandit probes that underperform on mixed workloads: short-chat prefills, long-document prefill bursts, and attention-phase switches (dense -> sparse attention) cause latency regressions and suboptimal cost. Goal: build a runtime component that combines population-based heuristics (particle/swarm-inspired exploration) with lightweight attention-phase probes and seqlen fingerprinting to recommend a kernel ensemble per request with cold-start warmstarts per tenant and safe fallback policies.
motivation: Several recent incidents and bench runs showed p99 regressions when requests switch attention patterns mid-prefill or when seqlen distribution deviates from historical percentiles. We need an online-autotuner that is robust across architectures (A100, H100, AMD) and supports quantized fallback kernels without user-visible latency spikes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end simulator shows >= 12% reduction in p99 latency across mixed workloads compared to baseline heuristic picker
Production canary (10% of requests on runtime-internal-canary) shows no increase in error rate and p99 latency regression < 2% for 72h
Cost-per-token for mixed workload cohort decreases by >= 6% after warmstart period
Fallback rate to safe-generic-kernel remains < 0.5% during steady-state
Unit tests and integration tests for probe lifecycle, warmstart cache, and fallback path merged
rollout_plan: 1) Offline: run simulator with historical traces and synthetic attention-phase switches
2) Unit/integration tests in CI with deterministic seeds
3) Canary: enable picker for 2 small service clusters with strict rollback hooks
4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 50% with daily SLO review
5) Full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics and manual signoff
safety_and_fallbacks: Hard SLO enforcement: if p95 or p99 increases beyond thresholds, immediately disable swarm exploration for affected cluster
Quantized-kernel compatibility table ensures API output parity within tolerance; otherwise route to verified kernel
Warmstart TTL and decay to prevent stale fingerprint biases
Probe budget per-request enforced (max 1 trial per 200 requests of same tenant)
experiment_plan: A) Compare pure Bayesian bandit vs. hybrid swarm+anneal approach in simulator across 3 seqlen distributions
B) Measure attention-phase probe effectiveness: introduce synthetic attention sparsity mid-prefill and record pick stability
C) Evaluate warmstart improvements using per-tenant microprofile cache vs. global cold start
D) Cost modeling: compute expected token-cost delta for each kernel ensemble choice
implementation_notes: Selector runs in the fast path: keep decision budget < 500us median overhead
Use compact seqlen fingerprint (3-pt histogram + recent-phase hash) to index warmstarts
Particle-swarm inspired explorer keeps N candidate kernel-ensembles and nudges weights using reward = -latency - alpha*cost + beta*stability
Annealing schedule reduces exploration for stable tenants; new tenants get higher initial temperature
Attention-phase probe is a micro-benchmark run at prefill start that tests dense vs. sparse matmul latency on the active kernel candidates
All learning state stored in shm with eviction policy to avoid cross-tenant leakage; persisted to tiered store for cross-host warmstart
Expose config flags: swarm_population, probe_budget, warmstart_ttl, anneal_rate
notes_and_links: Related tickets: ENG-712908 (kernel warmstart infra), ENG-67813 (probe harness improvements)

open_questions: How to encode cross-architecture kernel comparability in the reward function without overfitting to a single hardware percentile?

Storage: how frequently should warmstarts be persisted to avoid cold restarts for bursty tenants?
